parts.note: the frame that holds up a hanging is literally a support used in executions, not a supporter of the death penalty

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as backing for the death penalty as a policy; the cryptic reading is the physical structure that supports a hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: The scaffold frame used for hanging is quite literally a structure supporting an execution.

definitions.meaning: the first book that opens the Bible, the most famous volume
a British progressive rock band of that name, with Phil Collins and Peter Gabriel

explanation.surface: A well-known book's first chapter is meant for a band.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both the Bible's opening book and a famous rock band.

clue.text: The French veto against Asian country

parts.note: le is the French for the
a veto is a ban
on can mean against, as in leaning on a wall

explanation.surface: France's veto is used against a country in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Middle Eastern state on the Mediterranean, capital Beirut, lies in western Asia.

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men
to dock is to cut off, to lop

explanation.surface: Dockers on the quayside and sailors on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' suggests the harbour but is the verb to cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the lowest deck of a sailing ship, below the waterline.

clue.text: Vessel, part sunken, holds up unsupported

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top
holds means the run of letters is contained within the words vessel, part sunken

explanation.surface: A ship, partly sunk, somehow stays afloat with no support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' hides SSELPARTS in 'veSSEL PART Sunken'; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress or top with no shoulder ties has nothing holding it up, so it is unsupported in that sense.

clue.text: Element illuminated with current in buzz

parts.note: illuminated means lit

indicators.note: in tells us the current letter goes inside the word for buzz

parts.note: a buzz is a hum
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A chemist describes an element that is lit up and humming with electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the lightest metal in the periodic table, element number three.

indicators.note: raise in a down clue means the word is lifted up, read from bottom to top

parts.note: grand means regal, majestic

explanation.surface: Raise a glass for a grand drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale fizzy beer is a common drink ordered in pubs.

clue.text: Rapture seeing sunset finally passed pool?

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of the word sunset

parts.note: passed, as in time passed or ran by
pool is a cue game, an example of a sport, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Someone is enraptured watching the sunset over a pool.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a transport of delight is to be carried away with ecstasy.

indicators.note: rubbish as a verb means to trash, so these letters are messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Sunburn is dire, but you are covered.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with an insurance policy is covered against loss.

clue.text: Man who reportedly needs other people?

definitions.text: Man who reportedly needs other people?

parts.words: Man who reportedly needs other people?
parts.note: said out loud, needs is kneads: a man whose job is to knead other people's muscles

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sociable man; 'reportedly' turns needs into kneads, which is what a massage therapist does.
explanation.definitionFit: A male massage therapist works by kneading clients' bodies.

indicators.note: strangely signals that the letters are to be rearranged into an odd new order
almost means the word and loses its final letter, leaving AN

explanation.surface: Something looks oddly bluer and nearly like a cloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims AND to AN; 'Strangely' then rearranges BLUER plus AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A nebula is a vast interstellar cloud of gas and dust, so the adjective describes something hazy and cloud-like.

parts.note: G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: A grandmother's girls hand over a pair of spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles worn on the nose are commonly called by this plural name for lenses.

clue.text: Smooth singer's first with rubbish Queen

indicators.note: the singer's first means just the opening letter of the word singer

parts.note: with can mean and
pap is worthless rubbish, as in trashy reading matter
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A smooth singer opens a show beside some royal rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to rub a surface down with abrasive paper until it is even.

clue.text: Binge shows playing repeats every evening, initially

indicators.note: initially says to take the opening letter of each of the five words that follow binge

explanation.surface: A television binge: shows playing reruns night after night.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout of overindulgence, such as a shopping or drinking binge, is a synonym.

clue.text: Use vision, including nose oddly for feeling

indicators.note: including means the word for use vision wraps around the other letters

parts.note: to use vision is to see

indicators.note: oddly picks the first and third letters, the odd-numbered ones, of the word nose

explanation.surface: Use your eyes, and your nose too, to get a feel for things.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeling or perception, as in a sense of danger, is a synonym.

parts.note: the line taken by the Telegraph newspaper, its stated opinion in a leading article

explanation.walkthrough: A telegraph line suggests a cable for messages; here it is the stance of the Daily Telegraph, the newspaper printing this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's leading article sets out the paper's official line on an issue.

clue.text: Dress up bride with more fussing

indicators.note: fussing with something means fiddling it about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bridesmaids fuss over the bride, dressing her up even more.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress up a story means to embellish it with invented detail, just as decorative needlework embellishes cloth.

indicators.note: a bird for the table is dressed, prepared, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A game bird is fully dressed for the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game bird' reads as one phrase, but 'Game' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue sport played on a cloth-covered table with pockets is a game.

indicators.note: clutching means the word for gloomy holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: gloomy means dismal
one is I, so one's is I'S
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A gloomy figure clutches their own small bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' looks like a bag to go with 'clutching', but here it means the act of firing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given the sack is losing one's job, so the noun sack means the firing of an employee.

indicators.note: in means the letter for left goes inside the word for revolt

parts.note: to revolt is to defect, desert one's side

explanation.surface: Left-wing rebels swing round and change course.
explanation.definitionFit: To veer away from a set path is to turn aside, change direction.

parts.note: surfing on waves, surf for short
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A top water-sports expert rides the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: The top of something, its outer face, is the uppermost layer.

parts.note: the crown of something is its top

explanation.surface: The Crown is in charge of its subjects.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject under discussion is a theme or matter for conversation.

clue.text: Examine china dish missing lid's top

parts.note: china means mate or pal, from Cockney rhyming slang china plate = mate

indicators.note: missing means the dish loses a letter

parts.note: a plate is a dish

indicators.note: a lid's top is the first letter of the word lid

explanation.surface: Inspect a china dish with its lid's top missing.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate. 'missing' drops L from PLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors examine a body by feeling it with their hands.

clue.text: Body of church unchanged welcoming Son

indicators.note: welcoming means the phrase for unchanged takes the son letter inside

parts.note: unchanged means as is

explanation.surface: A church body stays unchanged as it welcomes a son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body' suggests a congregation, but it is a car's frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle's base frame or bodywork, the structure it is built on.

parts.note: for can mean because of, as in punished for lying
to work, of a machine, is to go

explanation.surface: Someone quits their post because of work.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign a claim or privilege is to give it up, to do without it.

clue.text: Quiet about Conservative, popular, facing a scrap

indicators.note: facing means set alongside, so the letter a follows directly
about means the word for quiet goes around the following letters

parts.note: quiet means still
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: A quiet politician faces a scrap with a popular Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places CIN inside STILL after its S; 'scrap' suggests a fight but means a tiny piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny trace or spark, as in not a whit of evidence, is a scrap.

definitions.meaning: casts off, as a snake does its skin
small wooden garden huts for storage

explanation.definitionFit: It means both casts off and garden huts used for storage.

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect the is shortened to t'
borders are ends, edges

explanation.surface: Someone looks after the county's borders.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire speakers famously clip 'the' to t', as in 'down t' pub'.
explanation.definitionFit: Caring for a garden or a patient is a synonym, as in nurse.

indicators.note: tips here means tips over, so the word for excluding is turned backwards

parts.note: save can mean except or excluding, as in all save one
the setter refers to themselves, so this compiler's is I'VE, short for I have

explanation.surface: The setter confesses that, leaving out the clues' tips, they have been misleading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips' looks like hints or ends to remove, but it is the turnaround signal on SAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An evasive answer dodges the truth, so it leads the hearer astray.

indicators.note: the fourth absconding means the fourth letter of the word for fugitives runs off and is removed

parts.note: fugitives are runaways

explanation.surface: A pursuer trails a band of fugitives after one of four escapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Runways are tracks or trails, such as the beaten paths animals use, as well as airstrips.

parts.note: bloomers suggests underwear but means young flowering plants, which a garden lattice holds up

explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' pretends to be the baggy knickers and supports a garment; really it is plants that bloom, trained up a garden frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice of wood strips is fixed in gardens so climbing flowers can grow up it.

clue.text: Checks after covering of safety procedures

indicators.note: after means the word for checks comes after the outer letters
the covering of a word is its outside, so take the first and last letters of safety

parts.note: to check a flow is to stem it

explanation.surface: Checks are done once the safety procedures are covered.
explanation.definitionFit: Methods or set ways of doing things are procedures, as in a filing scheme.
